$schema_doc: FIXTURE ONLY — NOT map data, NOT evidence about OSM (E10-T3). Drives the SAME runner (e2e/golden-routes/runner.test.ts) as the real curated set, but against the stub router e2e/golden-routes/stubValhalla.ts instead of a Valhalla graph, so that scripts/runbook-smoke.sh can prove the runbook's last step end-to-end: a data update that LOSES a height restriction must turn the Golden-Routes acceptance gate red. Coordinates are a fictional flat patch near 48°N/11°E that exists only inside the stub. The runner reads this file via GOLDEN_ROUTES_FILE, which no CI job sets; the structural gates in the runner always read the canonical e2e/golden-routes.json regardless, so this file can never make them pass vacuously. The stub models a through-road with a 3.2 m bridge at lon ~11.005 plus a northern bypass at lat ~48.004.

cases.provenance: FIXTURE: the stub's DIRECT path is a straight 0.01° lon segment at 48°N = ~745 m. Proves the runner's distance assertion runs end-to-end through the Core against the stub.

FIXTURE: the stub honours a modelled maxheight of 3.2 m. The 2.2 m profile is sent DIRECT (through forbidden_bbox); the 4.0 m profile is sent over the northern bypass. In STUB_REGRESSION=1 the stub ignores the height — exactly what a PBF that lost the maxheight tag would cause (W-08/W-17) — and this case MUST then fail. That inversion is the whole point of the runbook smoke test.

restriction.source: FIXTURE — modelled by e2e/golden-routes/stubValhalla.ts, not read from OSM

cases.provenance: FIXTURE: the stub plans the DIRECT path at 16 m/s, so ~745 m take ~47 s. The simulator then drives exactly that pace at speed_factor 1.0, which is docs/07 §3b's scenario in miniature — it exercises the whole route -> navigation/start -> simulator/play -> nav/state ETA -> arrival chain against a real Core in ~1 minute of wall clock instead of the several minutes the LI route needs.
